(2) FORMER FULL PROFESSORSHIP: Professor in the Department of Urology at Christian Medical College and Hospital, Vellore - one of India's most prestigious academic medical centres. A substantive professorial post is a strong standing signal. (3) SENIOR ROLE AT A SECOND MAJOR PRIVATE GROUP: previously Senior Consultant in Urology and Renal Transplantation at KIMS Hospital, Secunderabad (from around Apr 2017). (4) PREMIUM SPECIALTY MIX: kidney transplantation, robotic urological surgery, uro-oncology and andrology are among the highest-value service lines in Indian private healthcare; AIG's own urology department page advertises a kidney transplant team 'with exposure of more than 3000 kidney transplants' (this is a DEPARTMENT-level figure, explicitly NOT attributed to him personally - no individual procedure volume was published for him). (5) NATIONAL AWARDS AND FELLOWSHIP: winner of the Dr. R Sitaraman Memorial Essay Competition 2009, conducted by the Urological Society of India; recipient of the GM Phadke Travelling Fellowship, 2009. (6) ELITE TRAINING PEDIGREE: MBBS, SCB Medical College Cuttack; MS General Surgery, PGIMER Chandigarh; MCh Urology, JIPMER Puducherry - all top-tier national institutions. (7) MEDICAL-VALUE-TRAVEL VISIBILITY: carried on several international medical-tourism catalogues, which hospitals reserve for consultants they market to overseas patients. No evidence of an owned clinic or private practice brand.

notes: Distinctive name, so no ambiguity risk. Identity verified on name + specialty (Urology / renal transplantation, matching the row's 'Urology, Kidney Transplantation and Andrology') + hospital (AIG Hospitals) + city (Hyderabad/Gachibowli) via an AIG-owned doctor page plus his own LinkedIn headline 'Arabind Panda - Senior Consultant - AIG Hospitals', corroborated by Skedoc and HexaHealth which both place him at AIG Hospital Gachibowli. STALE-AFFILIATION CHECK PERFORMED (this row needed it): several medical-tourism catalogue pages still describe him as 'Senior Consultant in Urology and Renal Transplantation at KIMS Hospital Secunderabad', and one source dates that post to Apr 2017 onwards. AIG DOES publish him on its own domain and his own LinkedIn is current at AIG, so the stale-affiliation rule was NOT triggered - AIG is recorded as the current affiliation and KIMS plus his CMC Vellore professorship are captured in hni_signals as prior roles. A human should nonetheless be aware both hospitals appear in the open index. IMPORTANT URL WARNING - PLEASE READ BEFORE USING: across three separate queries, the search index repeatedly returned the URL https://aighospitals.com/doctor/dr-rohith-gorrepati under the TITLE 'Dr. Arabind Panda | Urology & Robotic Surgery Expert at AIG Hospitals'. That is a title/URL MISMATCH - the same URL was also returned under its own correct title, 'Dr. Rohith Gorrepati | Consultant Urologist at AIG Hospitals, Hyderabad'. The slug belongs to a DIFFERENT AIG urologist, so I deliberately did NOT record it as Dr Panda's profile despite the tempting title. Instead his genuine page surfaced separately through AIG's Google-translate locale mirror at .../doctor/dr-arabind-panda, and per rule 2 I recorded that URL exactly as returned rather than rewriting it to the canonical aighospitals.com form, which never appeared verbatim. A human can simply strip the translate wrapper. Also note aighospitals.com/doctors/dr-arabind-panda/ was returned as an explicit '404 Page Not Found' - that is the wrong pattern (plural /doctors/ WITH a trailing slash) and is not evidence he lacks a page. BAND = Medium: all AIG domains and locale mirrors count as ONE official source; LinkedIn is primary self-published and can never earn High; Skedoc, HexaHealth, Sehat, MyMedisage, Ortil, Doktors, Yashfiin and the medical-tourism catalogues are corroborating-only. healinindia.gov.in lists AIG urologist Dr. Bipin Chandra Pal but has NO listing for Dr Panda, so no independent official second source is available. NO CONTACT DETAILS EXIST PUBLICLY: no email, phone, mobile, personal website or clinic site surfaced across four queries - AIG publishes no per-doctor contact, so those fields are blank rather than guessed. The '3000+ kidney transplants' figure is a DEPARTMENT statistic from AIG's urology page and is explicitly not claimed as his personal volume.
